## [2.8.58] — 2026-07-02

### Fixed
- **Five engine defects surfaced by the issue-247 `/devflow:implement` dogfooding run are fixed, so consumer repos get faithful workpad AC mirrors, working post-merge classification, branch-mode deferral filing, a converging review that stops tripping its own gate, and clean doc-path extraction.** (1) `scripts/parse-acs.py`'s `_parse_checkboxes` now joins each checkbox item's indented continuation lines into one criterion before the post-merge scan, so a hard-wrapped acceptance criterion — the ~80-column format `/devflow:create-issue` emits — round-trips verbatim into the workpad and a post-merge trigger phrase sitting on a continuation line classifies correctly (previously each item was truncated to its first physical line). (2) Phase 4.0.5's deferral-manifest discovery (`skills/implement/phases/phase-4-documentation.md`) now searches both `.devflow/tmp/review/pr-<N>/` and the sanitized-current-branch slug directory (`/`→`-`, lowercased, non-`[a-z0-9._-]` dropped — the same convention `/devflow:review` uses), so a current-branch-mode `/devflow:review-and-fix` run's deferrals are no longer silently missed; the hydrated aggregate is still written at `pr-<N>/deferrals.json` where `/pr-description` reads it. (3) The post-shadow edit gate in `skills/review-and-fix/SKILL.md` now exempts a post-shadow commit whose diff touches only `.devflow/logs/**` (the engine's own observability artifacts, the same paths the review diff filter already strips), while any commit touching other paths still trips the gate — so the mandatory Loop-Exit `chore: persist review-and-fix observability artifacts` commit no longer forces a bounded delta-review on every writable converging run. (4) `scripts/extract-doc-needed-paths.sh` now keeps a token only when it ends in a recognized doc/source extension or names an in-tree file (`[ -f ]` plus `git ls-files`), dropping bare-directory tokens, rooted (`/…`) tokens unconditionally (an in-tree deliverable is always repo-relative, so even a rooted token that happens to name an existing file like `/README.md` is dropped), parent-dir-escaping (`../…`) tokens (so an out-of-tree `../notes.md` cannot slip through the extension branch), and skill-invocation references (e.g. `/claude-md-management`), so the Phase 4.1 deliverable gate consumes clean extractor output — the #247 body yields exactly `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `docs/install.md`.

### Added
- **The Phase 1.6 issue-claim audit gains Pass 4 — declared sequencing-dependency claims — and the DevFlow repo ships a `review-and-fix` prompt extension with two fail-open guard-class shapes.** Pass 4 (`skills/implement/phases/phase-1-setup.md`) extracts explicit `depends on / must merge after / blocked by / follow-up to #N` references from the issue body, checks each referenced issue's state via `gh issue view --json state`, records a confirmation note when all are closed or merged, and routes an open (or unresolvable) dependency to the Blocked path with the 👎 outcome reaction — so a run on a dependency-sequenced issue fails fast instead of building on unmerged work. `.devflow/prompt-extensions/review-and-fix.md` sharpens the fix-delta gate and shadow reviewer prompts with the existence-vs-sourceability shape (`[ -f file ] && . file` fails open when the sibling exists but is unreadable/corrupt — verify the outcome, e.g. `type <fn>`, not the precondition) and the tr-dependence shape (a value derived through an external PATH tool like `tr` silently degrades where the tool is absent), each carrying its #247 reproduction. Covered by a wrapped-AC parser test in `lib/test/test_python_scripts.py`, the #247 extractor fixture, and `lib/test/run.sh` pins for the branch-slug discovery arm, the post-shadow logs-only exemption and its counter-assertion, and Pass 4 presence. (#255, closes #254)
- **The shared review verdict engine now REJECTs a PR that contradicts its own diff at *every* `verdict_severity_threshold` — a threshold- and severity-independent self-contradicting-diff carve-out, symmetric with the one `#251` placed in `receiving-code-review`.** `#251` made the REJECT line configurable by severity but added no notion of scope or self-contradiction, so the mechanical escape behind the original `lenient-verdict` retrospective stayed open in the *verdict* engine: a finding that a doc/release-note line, a code comment, or a test **the PR's own diff added or modified** is untrue could be relabeled "pre-existing / out-of-scope / Informational" (or demoted via a Phase 4.0 deferral match) and thereby demoted out of the REJECT set, letting a self-falsifying PR earn a non-REJECT verdict. `skills/review/SKILL.md` Phase 4.2 now carries a carve-out **evaluated before the numbered rules**: such a finding drives REJECT at every threshold value (including the default `critical`) and regardless of the severity chip the agent assigned it (a Suggestion-graded self-contradiction still REJECTs); it is **non-demotable** (Phase 4.0's deferral-demotion step and the 4.1 report-rendering rule both explicitly exclude it — only a *fix* clears the REJECT) and **corroboration-independent** (a single-source self-contradicting finding blocks exactly like a corroborated one). Rule 3 gains an in-scope qualifier mirroring the existing `type-design-analyzer` "diff does not touch" carve-out — when the threshold admits Important, an admitted finding does not REJECT if it is genuinely pre-existing behavior the diff does not touch — which the self-contradicting carve-out overrides (such a finding is always in-scope). The Phase 4.1 "Verdict Criteria" summary and Phase 4.4's `--request-changes` mapping are updated in lockstep; the carve-out shares its definition of "contradicts the diff" (a claim that is stale, contradicts HEAD, or contradicts another part of this change) with the `receiving-code-review` documented-falsehood carve-out. At the default `critical`, verdict computation for findings that do not contradict the diff is byte-identical to today; the only default-threshold change is that a self-contradicting-diff finding drives REJECT instead of being demotable to a note, and the Phase 4.1.5 over-grade advisory annotation is unchanged. `/devflow:review-and-fix` inherits the carve-out automatically via the engine-sharing contract, and `#251`'s REJECT-driver-always-fixable widening rule already routes a self-contradicting finding to the fixer so its loop must fix (never defer) it to converge. Engine-only: no application code, **no new config key/schema property/example entry**. Enforced by seven coupled `lib/test/run.sh` operative-sentence/coupled-site pins (A1–A7, including a dedicated pin for the corroboration-independence clause); `docs/DEVFLOW_SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md`'s verdict paragraph documents the carve-out. (#276, closes #263)

## [2.8.57] — 2026-07-02

### Added
- **`/devflow:create-issue` now handles the visual specification of user-visible UI changes, so UI/frontend issues carry a real screenshot/mockup or an explicitly-verified placement spec instead of an ambiguous text description.** The skill previously produced text-only issues with no awareness of visual artifacts — it never checked for a supplied screenshot, never asked for one, and never verified placement/layout/states — leaving the downstream `/devflow:implement` to guess where a UI element goes and how it looks. Step 2 of `skills/create-issue/SKILL.md` gains a **Visual-specification guidance** clause (prose guidance the orchestrator follows, **not** a new hard gate, consistent with the existing Step-2 clarification model): the orchestrator (1) **infers** whether the issue involves user-visible UI as part of its normal scope assessment — no dedicated "is this UI?" question; (2) on a UI change, **checks the user-provided resources/context** (pasted images, attached files, URLs, design-tool links such as Figma) for an existing screenshot/mockup; (3) **records** a present screenshot in the new Visual Specification section (embedded when a hosted URL exists, otherwise referenced with an obtain-note); (4) **asks** for one when none is present; (5) when the user has none, **verbally verifies** the visual details before finalizing — placement & layout, visual states (hover/focus/error/empty/loading/disabled), responsive behavior across breakpoints, and design-system/style match, as a **non-exhaustive** prompt the orchestrator extends per task; and (6) **writes** the screenshot reference and/or verified placement description into the section. A screenshot is **preferred, not mandatory** — verbal verification is an accepted substitute — and an unresolved UI-placement detail at user disengagement flows to the existing `## 🚫 Blocked` section (the existing mechanism, not a new gate). **Non-UI issues skip the whole path and gain no new questions.** `skills/create-issue/references/issue-template.md` gains the rendered-only-for-UI **Visual Specification** section plus a matching Quality-checklist line, and `docs/DEVFLOW_SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md` §11 mirrors the behavior — the three are a coupled site kept mutually consistent. Pinned in `lib/test/run.sh` (an 11-assertion `#272` block: the template section heading + its Quality-checklist line as a coupled-pin, the SKILL.md Step-2 UI-detection / resource-check / record-embed-or-reference / ask-when-absent / verbal-verification-dimensions / preferred-not-mandatory / non-UI-skip / Blocked-route guidance, and the §11 mirror — one pin per acceptance criterion, each RED against the pre-change state). Markdown/skill-body change only; no runtime code, dependency, or config key. (#273, closes #272)
- **`/devflow:implement`'s review engine now forces an auditable operative-sentence note on every behavioral-fix pin and deterministically persists `review-and-fix` observability artifacts when the loop is driven inline.** Two independent weaknesses on the `/devflow:implement` review surface let a defect ship "green," caught only by a blinded shadow pass or not at all. (A) The contract-pin discipline — pin the *operative* sentence whose removal *alone* re-introduces the bug, never an adjacent *framing/justification* clause — was prose advice a fix-iteration author could quietly violate by pinning the nearest unique literal (the recurring framing-only-pin class behind PRs #173/#171/#167). It is now a forced auditable artifact: before writing any behavioral-fix pin, the author records a one-line workpad `--note` naming the operative sentence and asserting the pin literal is a substring of it — the same auditable-commitment idiom as the Phase 2.3 sweep-selection and test-first notes — required at both co-equal author sites (`skills/implement/phases/phase-2-implement.md` §2.3 and `skills/review-and-fix/SKILL.md`'s Step 3 mutation-check step) and scoped to behavioral-fix pins only, never literal-constant/token-name/count/absence pins. (B) `review-and-fix`'s Loop Exit writes each run's effectiveness record (`.devflow/logs/efficiency/<slug>-<run-id>.json`) and durable workpad copy from its per-iteration `iter-*.json`; when Phase 3.3 reproduces that loop **inline** — its normal mode — a dropped Loop Exit left those artifacts unwritten and the run contributed nothing to `.devflow/logs/efficiency/` (`review-and-fix`'s own #1 "Common Mistake," unguarded at this seam). Phase 3.3 now, after each inline `review-and-fix` invocation returns (both the first pass and the bounded re-review) and regardless of verdict, runs the existing idempotent `lib/efficiency-trace.sh --persist` Layer-3 backstop against a freshly-taken this-run snapshot, and records a `dropped-failed` reflection both when `--persist` has no `iter-*.json` inputs at all and when it has inputs but its own record derivation/write step failed (detected via either of its two distinct failure breadcrumbs — the jq/mkdir `record not written` shape and the differently-worded disk/permission write-failure shape) — so a telemetry loss is surfaced in the common cases this backstop covers, rather than silently absent. Both new clauses are enforced by coupled `lib/test/run.sh` removal-proof pins (`assert_pin_red_on_removal`); no new script, dependency, config key, or workflow change (the shared skill body reaches both the local and cloud `/devflow:implement` tiers, and `lib/efficiency-trace.sh` is already allowlisted). `docs/implement-skill.md` describes both guards. (#236, closes #235)

## [2.8.56] — 2026-07-02

### Fixed
- **The `/devflow:implement` workpad's `## Plan` and `## Acceptance Criteria` self-record can no longer read as interim on a genuinely-complete run — the terminal `Status: Complete` write is now a deterministic reconciliation chokepoint.** Two related defects left completed runs with `- [ ]` rows whose work actually shipped — (1) the only `--tick-plan` loop lived in Phase 2, so the two Plan steps that complete in **Phase 3** (the version-bump/`CHANGELOG` entry and the final full-suite/`shellcheck`/`ruff` run) were chronically left unticked; and (2) the Phase 3.4 AC gate's "every non-post-merge AC is `- [x]`" check was prose-only/LLM-enforced, so a run could advance with the last AC row still `- [ ]` — while (3) the Phase 4.3 finalize flipped `Status: Complete` without ever re-checking the self-record, so nothing deterministic caught either drift. `scripts/workpad.py` now, **only** on a `--status Complete` mutation and over the *post-mutation* sections (so a call that ticks the last AC and flips to Complete in one shot still passes), scans the checkbox sections: any **non-post-merge** `## Acceptance Criteria` row still `- [ ]` is a **structural failure** — the whole call aborts non-zero with **no PATCH** and `Status` is not flipped, naming each offending row on stderr — mirroring the existing structural-abort contract (`(post-merge)`-tagged rows are excluded byte-for-byte as in the Phase 3.4 gate); any still-unticked `## Plan` row emits a **non-blocking** stderr warning and the Complete write otherwise succeeds (a genuinely dropped/superseded step may honestly stay unticked). A Complete write whose `## Acceptance Criteria` section still holds the un-mirrored `new-body` placeholder (AC-mirroring never ran, so the hard-fail scan has no rows to check) likewise emits a **non-blocking** warning rather than passing silently — a genuinely AC-less issue carries the distinct `_(none provided in issue body)_` sentinel and is unaffected. The gate **never** auto-ticks a row — auto-ticking incomplete work would make the self-record lie — and never fires for `--status Blocked`, any non-`Complete` status, or a status-less update. Phase 3 (`skills/implement/phases/phase-3-review.md`) gains an explicit §3.5 instructing the orchestrator to `--tick-plan` the version-bump/`CHANGELOG` and final-suite Plan rows at the point their work completes, and Phase 4.3 (`skills/implement/phases/phase-4-documentation.md`) documents the new structural-abort as a distinct non-zero finalize exit. Pinned in `lib/test/run.sh` (a 5-scenario CLI block: AC hard-fail with no PATCH, post-merge-only success, Plan warning, all-ticked silence, `--status Blocked` un-gated — the AC-hard-fail and Plan-warning scenarios go RED against the pre-change helper, the other three are controls that pass identically on both to guard against the gate over-firing) and `lib/test/test_python_scripts.py` (adding the post-mutation-ordering, AC-precedence-over-Plan, and un-mirrored-placeholder-warning cases). (#265, closes #258)

## [2.8.55] — 2026-07-02

### Added
- **Reusable primitives for a cloud `/devflow:implement` stall backstop — the deterministic core that detects a headless run which ended mid-lifecycle yet reported success.** A headless single-shot `claude-code-action` run can stop the moment the model emits a tool-call-free turn (e.g. right after `gh pr create`), leaving the workpad frozen at an interim `Status` while the job goes green — indistinguishable from a healthy completion (#259→#264, #258→#265). The agent-side terminal-status self-check cannot fire once the session has ended, so a workflow-level backstop is the only deterministic guard. This change ships the self-contained, fully-tested primitives that backstop is built from: `scripts/stall-backstop-decide.sh` (a pure decision core mapping `{enabled, status-class, attempts, cap}` to `skip|noop|resume|fail-exhausted|fail-unreadable`, extracted so it is unit-testable outside the workflow YAML); `scripts/post-issue-comment.sh` (a best-effort, repo-scoped REST issue-comment helper mirroring the `ensure-label.sh`/`apply-labels.sh` always-exit-0 + stderr-breadcrumb contract, so a comment hiccup never flips a gate); a `workpad.py status` read subcommand that reports the workpad `Status` as `CLASS GLYPH WORD` reusing the single-source glyph vocabulary (exit 2 = no workpad, exit 1 = present-but-unreadable, so a caller fails closed); and the `devflow_implement.stall_backstop.{enabled,max_resume_attempts}` config keys (example + schema, `additionalProperties: false`, safe-direction defaults `true`/`2`). `lib/test/run.sh` pins every decision branch, the helper contracts, and the config peer set, each RED against the pre-change state. The thin workflow caller in `.github/workflows/devflow-implement.yml` that wires these together (plus its workflow-behavior test pins and the AC11 `.github`-freeze reconciliation) is **deferred to a follow-up**: pushing a `.github/workflows` edit requires a `workflows:write` token (the optional `DEVFLOW_APP_ID` App) this run's token lacks — the same `.github`-freeze deferral pattern used for the 2.8.54 jq-wrapper migration. (#267, part of #266)
## [2.8.54] — 2026-07-02
